FLAG_A.definition: FIRES only if a paper writes base-model hidden states (residual, attention outputs or KV cache) into the forward pass of its tuned descendant at inference and reports a change in output or solution diversity. Logit/token mixing, weight interpolation, training, base-derived directions for other behaviours, and instruct-to-base transfer are adjacent.

decisive_sentence.quote: At evaluation, the hidden state entering the late boundary is replaced for all sequence positions and the downstream stack recomputes its own keys and values.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Writes base upstream states into the descendant's late stack (all positions) with boundary and token controls, but the outcome is a next-token target margin at the first base/descendant divergence, not output or solution diversity. Rubric total 2.5 = occupies B1's METHOD.

decisive_sentence.quote: By replacing the fine-tuned model’s activations with the corresponding base model activations, we assess the effectiveness of this technique in mitigating the backdoor.
decisive_sentence.section: Sec. 4.4 (Switch from Fine-tuned to Base Models)

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Base activations patched into the fine-tuned (backdoored) model; outcome = backdoor trigger rate, not diversity.

decisive_sentence.quote: We further conduct cross-model experiments by patching hidden representations from base to post (forward patching) and from post to base (backward patching).

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Base-to-post patching of knowledge representations; outcome = factual log-probability ratio.

decisive_sentence.quote: we hypothesize that mode collapse can be localized to specific layers and that restoring a carefully chosen range of layers to their pre-trained weights can recover diversity while maintaining high output quality.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Diversity outcome, but restores pre-trained WEIGHTS of a layer interval (weight level, adjacent by definition).

decisive_sentence.quote: This approach combines the lower layers of an aligned model with the higher layers of its base model based on the hypothesis that lexical diversity is more closely associated with lower layers and semantic diversity with higher layers.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Diversity outcome, but a layer splice of weights (aligned lower + base higher), the reverse composition.

decisive_sentence.quote: Guided by this localization, layer interpolation restores entrance diversity and increases solution coverage by 37%, with pass@1 of 0.305 versus 0.278 for the late policy.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Solution-family diversity restored by layer interpolation (weights) and by text entrance prefixes; Countdown, not code; abstract only.

decisive_sentence.quote: At inference time, ReDiverse-TF introduces a training-free mechanism that steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Diversity restored by steering a distilled student along teacher directions: diffusion models, not a base->tuned LLM transplant.

FLAG_A.consequence_for_wording: The word 'first' is NOT permitted for writing base-model states into a tuned descendant (cross-model patching exists: Prakash et al. 2024; Oozeer et al. 2025; Du et al. 2025; Zhou 2026 cross-patching). Permitted: 'to our knowledge (dated search 2026-10-21), no prior work writes base-model prefill states into the instruct model to test whether post-training's narrowing of solution (algorithm) choice is carried by those states; cross-model patching of base states exists for other outcomes, and base/aligned mixing for diversity exists at the token, logit and weight level.'

FLAG_B.definition: FIRES if a paper predicts, per prompt or per task and from the base model's own distribution, either where post-training narrows or whether/where the tuned model can be steered. PARTLY FIRED if the prediction is per-problem but at training time or for correctness coverage only, or stylised without a per-task test.

decisive_sentence.quote: decompose prompts by frozen base-model behavior into solved-easy, reachable, boundary, and out-of-reach regimes, turning an aggregate pass@k curve into an attribution problem.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Per-prompt forecast from frozen-base evidence of where GRPO loses coverage: training time, correctness coverage (math). PARTLY FIRED by the frozen rule.

decisive_sentence.quote: A priori signals capture a minority of it: base pass rate, the likelihood of a correct solution, a larger model’s pass rate and their combinations explain only 0.30 [...] and 0.24 [...] of the explainable variance in gains.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Per-problem forecast of post-training gains from base pass rate / likelihood: training time, correctness; the base signals explain only a minority of the explainable variance (contradicts-in-part).

decisive_sentence.quote: Lookahead outperforms BoN at predicting which IFEval prompts degrade after training

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Per-prompt forecast of post-training degradation from base model + reward model: training time.

decisive_sentence.quote: we track a forward-only signal: the per-prompt decay rate λ̂ of the likelihood of frozen base-correct trajectories on boundary prompts, those the base model solves only rarely.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Per-prompt decay of base-correct likelihood forecasts RLVR damage during training; random-prompt anchoring protects as well.

decisive_sentence.quote: RLVR disproportionately reinforces problems with high likelihood, correct solutions under the base model while suppressing other initially low-likelihood ones.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Base likelihood orders which problems RLVR reinforces vs suppresses (mechanism; anchor outside window).

decisive_sentence.quote: sharpens the reference distribution, amplifying its modes while suppressing the tails. The effect strengthens as typicality bias
decisive_sentence.section: App. D.3 (Power-Transform Sharpening under Typicality Bias)

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Stylised: aligned optimum = power-sharpened reference policy; no per-task test (PARTLY FIRED: stylised).

decisive_sentence.quote: the nucleation phase caused by supervised finetuning, in which behavior collapses onto a single seed distribution present in the pretrained LLM; and (3) a settling phase in which reinforcement learning techniques redistribute probability of the collapsed distribution, but largely keep it concentrated on the same options as the seed distribution.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: SFT collapses onto a seed distribution already present in the pretrained model; retrospective, random-generation tasks.

decisive_sentence.quote: 92.9% of post-training Top-1 changes remain within the pretrained Top-16 on average, while their relative preferences are substantially reorganized.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Post-training top-1 changes mostly stay within the base top-16 (retrospective, token level).

FLAG_B.consequence_for_wording: A1 may not claim to be the first to predict from the base model where post-training narrows: training-time, per-prompt forecasts of coverage loss from frozen-base evidence exist (Zhou 2026; Duan 2026; Lookahead). A1's defensible addition is an INFERENCE-TIME forecast of the tuned model's movability on algorithm choice from the base model's per-task algorithm distribution, scored on matched events. A2 (where a push or ban lands = the base model's runner-up) has only stylised/retrospective support (power-sharpening; base top-k inheritance; seed-distribution collapse) and may be worded 'to our knowledge'.

FLAG_C.definition: FIRES if a paper measures algorithm-level diversity of test-checked code in a base model against its tuned descendant. PARTLY FIRED if the comparison exists but with an LLM-judge clustering, a single pair, or a mixed direction.

decisive_sentence.quote: When comparing the Deepseek-base and Deepseek-instruct models, algorithmic diversity shows different patterns: instruction tuning decreases algorithmic diversity in AtCoder-introductory problems, but increases it in other problems.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Base vs Instruct DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B, test-checked correctness, LLM-judge (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) algorithm clusters, one pair, MIXED direction (decrease on easy AtCoder-introductory problems, increase elsewhere).

decisive_sentence.quote: Relative to the corresponding base model, Base-RLVR decreases JPlag diversity in 57.2% [...] of comparisons and decreases Vendi score in 65.3% [...] of comparisons.

candidates.why_not_full_fire: Base vs RLVR descendants on code with execution tests; structural (JPlag) and embedding (Vendi) diversity, not algorithm-level.

decisive_sentence.quote: For RQ1, we show that uncontrolled sampling (for 24 LLMs) yields considerably less diverse solutions than human solutions

candidates.why_not_full_fire: DivAlgo (24 code models) has NO base-vs-instruct pairing (checked by grep on the full text); included here as a negative check.

FLAG_C.consequence_for_wording: Strike 'first base-versus-tuned algorithm-level comparison'. The premise row reads 'contradicting in part' (Lee et al. find instruction tuning increases algorithmic diversity on harder problems). The run may claim test-checked mechanism labels over correct programs (runtime tracer, AST, blind judge) rather than LLM-judge clusters, a per-task base repertoire committed by sha256 before any push, and the same chat-templated prompt for base and instruct (with the template confound flagged by Nakamura 2026).
